T h is application coming on for admission this day, t h e co
 following:

Order 
This second bail application under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure has been filed by the applicant for grant of regular bail in relation to FIR No. 407/2023 dated 14.05.2023, registered at Police Station Nishatpura, District Bhopal (M.P.) for commission of offence under Sections 498A,
304B/34 of IPC.
Applicant is in detention since 14.05.2023.

2. Applicant's first bail application under Section 439 of Cr.P.C. was dismissed on merit vide order dated 03.10.2023 passed in M.Cr.C. No.43451/2023.
3.
As per the prosecution story, on 11.04.2023, deceased Saroj wife of Anil Rai committed suicide by hanging herself in matrimonial home.
Her marriage was performed with Anil Rai on 14.05.2021.

In the course of inquiry and investigation it was alleged that husband along with his elder brother and mother-in-law were harassing and torturing the deceased in connection with demand of one Alto car and gold chain.
It is further alleged that on account of cruelty caused by aforesaid persons with the deceased, deceased committed suicide.
After investigation, charge sheet has been filed.

sentences.text: This second bail application has been filed only on the ground that witnesses have not turned up before the trial Court for tendering of evidence despite issuance of summons to them.
Therefore, it is prayed that applicant may be released on bail.

5. Learned counsel for the applicant has placed reliance on Roopa @ Ramroop vs. State of M.P.
reported in ILR (2012) M.P., 657, in which bail was granted.

entities.text:
Roopa @ Ramroop vs. State of M.P.
reported in ILR (2012) M.P., 657
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 6. On the other hand, learned counsel for the respondent/State has opposed grant of bail and has submitted that deceased marriage was performed with the applicant on 14.05.2021.
She committed suicide hanging herself in matrimonial home where she was residing with the applicant husband.
She has died within two years of marriage under mysterious condition.
Therefore, he has prayed for rejection of the bail application.

7. In this case, parents have made specific allegations that their daughter was being harassed,
tortured and beaten in connection with demand of one Alto car, one gold chain and other articles.
The continuous demand of dowry compelled the deceased/newly married wife to commit suicide.
Mere non-appearance of the witnesses on 3-4 occasions cannot said to be a delay in trial.
Charge-sheet has been filed only 6-7 months ago.
Therefore, no case for grant of bail on ground of delay is made out.
8. As far as the case law relied on by the learned counsel for the applicant is concerned, that is a bail order and bail orders are not precedent.
Therefore, no benefit can be given to the applicant on the basis of the aforesaid bail order.
Consequently, having taken into consideration the heinousness of offence and other facts and circumstances of the case, I am of the view that no case for grant of bail is made out.
Consequently, this second bail application too under Section 439 of Cr.P.C. filed on behalf of the applicant is dismissed.

(DINESH KUMAR PALIWAL) JUDGE ak Anil Rai vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 12 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/185693763/
